supported_scope: Setting execution modes with different file operation behaviors; sandbox containment for terminal commands; permission modes governing command execution; interactive diff review and approval for file writes
unestablished_scope: Hard enforcement of limits vs. warnings or instruction-based requests
required_setup: Configure execution mode via settings.json or CLI flags; optionally enable terminal sandbox in settings.json; configure toolPermission mode for safety barriers; optionally override permissions.allow rules for headless mode
constraints: Sandbox is an OS-level containment feature and must be enabled in settings.json
Permission modes affect whether commands require user approval or run automatically
Execution mode affects file write behavior: default mode pauses for review, accept-edits auto-approves, plan mode prepends /plan prefix
Headless mode disables interactive prompts and relies on policy and pre-granted permissions

evidence.section: Choose an execution mode > Available modes
evidence.quote: default Pauses for interactive diff review before modifying or creating files. Standard development, reviewing sensitive code changes, and careful refactoring.
evidence.claim: Execution modes provide different levels of file operation control including pausing for review.

evidence.quote: The terminal sandbox is a lightweight security isolation mechanism that protects your host system from potentially destructive file manipulations or unauthorized outbound network requests when the agent executes local shell commands.
evidence.claim: Terminal sandbox provides containment to limit execution impact.

evidence.section: CLI best practices > Configure your workspace environment > Establish structured permissions
evidence.quote: Tune your safety barriers in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json based on your project risk level: request-review (default): Prompts you before executing any write operations, Bash commands, or remote network calls.
evidence.claim: Permission modes govern interactive approval for command execution.

evidence.section: Headless mode > Permissions in headless mode
evidence.quote: By default, the CLI respects the permission mode in your settings. A tool that requires approval it can’t obtain is soft-denied: the run continues, exits 0 , and prints a notice to stderr naming the tool and how to allow it.
evidence.claim: In headless mode, permission approvals are handled by policy with soft-denies for unapproved tools.
